title: Adaptive keyhashing, TTL annealing, and rollback orchestration for KV prefix caching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Static TTLs and monolithic cache keys are causing cost regressions when traffic shifts between long-tail and hot prefixes. We need an automated recommendation and safe-apply system that can: 1) compute per-prefix confidence-scored TTL suggestions using observed hit-rate curves; 2) split/rehash heavy prefixes into sharded cache keys to avoid hot-key blowups; 3) schedule TTL "annealing" (gradual TTL adjustments) and staged rollouts with automatic rollback triggers tied to latency/hitrate/cost metrics.

Goal: Deliver an opinionated module plus orchestration flow that generates recommended config changes, runs a deterministic dry-run simulation against a traffic replay, and applies changes via a staged canary (1% -> 10% -> 100%) with automated safety gates and a one-button rollback that is safe for in-flight KV usage and batching behavior.
comments: 2026-01-11 - Kickoff: scoped to runtime + console UX for recommendations. Agreed to use offline replay for initial validation (Maya, Diego, Priya).
2026-01-18 - Prototype notebooks show TTL annealing reduces cold-miss storms in simulated shard configs; baseline cost down ~12% on replay for the ACME prompt corpus (diego/priya).
2026-01-25 - Design review: decided to use a 3-phase annealing window (gradual TTL increase/decrease over 24h) and to bind safety gates to both hit-rate and p99 latency. PM okayed P1 priority (Sam).
2026-01-30 - Implementation: added deterministic keyhash sharding library and a config schema extension: 'shard_count', 'ttl_schedule', 'confidence_score' (Diego).
2026-02-03 - Integration test: dry-run traffic replay integrated with the policy simulator; noticed interaction with batching — sharding increased batch variance, added batch-preserve hint (Maya).
2026-02-08 - In-progress: building console UI for accept/reject diff and one-click rollback. Preparing PR and internal benchmark dashboard link.
implementation_notes: Recommendation engine computes per-prefix exponential hit-rate curves and derives a TTL suggestion + confidence score using a Bayesian smoothing prior.
Keyhash sharding uses a deterministic Murmur3-based hash with configurable 'shard_count' per prefix and a routing table that preserves locality for batching when possible.
TTL annealing applies a time series schedule: candidate TTL changes are introduced at low weight and gradually ramped up if safety gates pass at each checkpoint.
Config apply is atomic at the metadata-plane level; runtime nodes pickup config versions and evaluate per-request whether to route through old/new cache key logic to avoid double-miss races.
Added 'batch-preserve' hint to the shard metadata to prefer grouping requests with same logical prefix into same batch slice when shard_count>1.
Expose diagnostics: estimated tokens saved, simulated hit-rate delta, simulated cost delta, and expected latencies for each rollout step.
Console UX will show a diff, cost projection, and preflight replay results before the team can kick off canary phases.
test_plan: Unit tests for keyhash sharder and TTL scheduler with synthetic prefix distributions.
Replay tests using three customer traces (ACME, EcomSim, InternalBench) to validate simulated hit-rate and cost projections.
End-to-end staging deploy: staged canary 1%/10%/100% against synthetic traffic with rollback triggers enabled.
Chaos test: kill a subset of runtime nodes mid-rollout to validate safe in-flight handling and eventual consistency of config versioning.
Performance test: ensure batching variance increase due to sharding stays <5% p95 latency regression.
Acceptance gating: pass replay accuracy (simulated vs actual hit rate delta < 2%) and cost savings projection within 15% of observed.
rollback_plan: Immediate automated rollback if any of the following are breached within 60 minutes of a rollout step: p99 latency increase > 5% absolute, hit-rate drop > 6% absolute, estimated cost per 1k tokens increase > 10%.

Manual rollback button in Console that triggers an atomic metadata version revert and signals runtime nodes to read the previous keying strategy; runtime uses a quick-merge path to avoid double fetches.
If rollback occurs during an anneal window, freeze anneal scheduler for 24h and run additional replay tests before reattempting.
Post-rollback incident runbook: collect replay logs, top-100 prefixes by miss delta, and re-evaluate shard_count suggestions. Assign incident owner for remediation.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine generates TTL + shard_count suggestions for 95% of observed prefixes in the replay traces.
Dry-run replay predicts >=8% median cost savings on ACME trace and no more than 3% p99 latency regression in simulation.
Staged canary flow completes with automated safety gates and no false-positive rollbacks in staging; one successful rollout to 100% in staging.
Console UI shows clear diff, cost projection, and allows one-click rollback. Docs and runbook updated.
